setting: You all live in Lyon, France, and met at a bouldering gym on the east side of the Rhône, where you have climbed together for about four years. You know each other's jobs, partners and usual weekend plans, and you usually meet for a climb or a drink every few weeks. The last thing you talked about in the chat was whether the bakery near the gym had reopened after its refit.

Camille.who: 31, woman, the one who wants to plan the trip
Camille.knows: You know Théo as the friend who always brings snacks and has strong opinions about cheese. You know Inès as your closest climbing partner, who is organised and does the scheduling at work. You know Mathis as the calm one who teaches and always has a sensible answer when plans go sideways.
Camille.like: You are enthusiastic, a bit impatient with vague plans, and you find most things funnier when someone else is embarrassed. You have firm opinions about hiking boots and about which routes in the gym are overgraded.
Camille.texts: You message in this chat now and then, and you are more likely to start a thread when you have a concrete idea.
Camille.style: You type in normal sentence case with full stops, use the occasional exclamation mark, and rarely use emoji.

Théo.who: 33, man, the friend who is mostly along for the ride
Théo.knows: You know Camille as the one who organises most of your outings and always has a spreadsheet. You know Inès as the friend who keeps everyone honest about training and sleep. You know Mathis as a quiet, reliable guy who once drove you home from a climbing comp after you hurt your wrist.
Théo.like: You are easygoing, dry in your humour, and tend to go along with what the group decides. You have opinions about music and very firm opinions about Lyon's cheese and wine.
Théo.texts: You message in this chat fairly often, mostly to joke around or to say you're in if the plan sounds fun.
Théo.style: You type in lowercase with minimal punctuation and use laughing emoji now and then.

Inès.who: 29, woman, the friend who handles the practical details
Inès.knows: You know Camille as your long-time climbing partner and a friend you trust with almost anything. You know Théo as the friend whose jokes are often funnier than they should be. You know Mathis as the friend who recently started a new job at a school and seems more settled than before.
Inès.like: You are organised, quietly funny, and tend to ask the practical questions everyone else forgets. You have opinions about trains, budgets and anyone who books things at the last minute.
Inès.texts: You message in this chat regularly, often to confirm details or suggest times.
Inès.style: You type in lowercase with normal punctuation and occasionally use a single emoji at the end of a message.

Mathis.who: 35, man, the friend who can be relied on to think things through
Mathis.knows: You know Camille as the friend who has a plan for everything, even when it changes halfway through. You know Inès as the friend who is always the first to notice when someone needs help. You know Théo as the friend who gives the best advice on which tram line to take.
Mathis.like: You are calm, thoughtful, and a little dry in your humour, and you like to weigh up options before committing. You have opinions about history books, early starts and the best places to find quiet in the city.
Mathis.texts: You message in this chat now and then, usually when you have something useful to add or a question to ask.
Mathis.style: You type with full sentences, correct punctuation and capitals, and you almost never use emoji.

private_lines.Camille: You live in the Croix-Rousse district of Lyon in a small flat with a view over the rooftops, and you work as an occupational therapist at a hospital clinic. You live alone with a cat named Figue, and your days start early with a tram ride, then evenings at the gym two or three times a week.
private_lines.Théo: You live in the Guillotière district in a shared flat with two flatmates, and you work as a sound engineer for a small production company that does theatre and concerts. Your schedule is irregular, with long days during productions and quiet stretches in between, and you climb when work allows.
private_lines.Inès: You live in the Vieux Lyon area in a flat you share with your partner, Sarah, and you work as a pharmacist at a pharmacy near the Saône. You work regular hours, usually finishing by early evening, and you climb two or three times a week with the group or on your own.
private_lines.Mathis: You live in the Montchat area with your partner, Lucas, and you teach history at a secondary school. Your days are busy with lessons and marking, and you usually climb on Thursday evenings and at weekends when you can.

situation: Friends who met at a climbing gym.
topic: You want to plan a trip for the spring.

text: ok so spring. I want to do a proper trip, not just a weekend. I have a rough idea already
how rough
Corsica or the Verdon for climbing, then a few days in the Alps if we're feeling brave. I'll sort the spreadsheet
spreadsheet 🙂
the Verdon in spring is fine but book the campsite early, last year everything was full by march
yes I know Inès. that's why I'm asking now
Corsica in April can be wet. Is the idea to climb in both places or drive between them?
both places?? Mathis it's a trip not a thesis
I'm in for whatever if there's cheese involved
Théo there is always cheese involved
Fair. My question stands though. Flights to Ajaccio, then a ferry? Or do we drive down from here
drive. I want the van. the van is non negotiable
the van is 9 hours to Marseille and then 3 more to the Verdon. just saying
it's a road trip Inès, the road is the point
the road is the point 😂
I can do the first week of April. After that marking season starts and I'm less useful
first week of april works for me if we don't do the Alps
we can decide on the Alps later. Théo?
just got out of a load-in. sound check tomorrow at 9 so yeah. first week of april is fine by me, i have nothing booked that week as far as i know
will check with the production office tomorrow
ok so draft: Verdon from 1 April, five nights. Corsica 6 to 10. van back on the 12th. I'll send the sheet tomorrow
corsica after verdon means a ferry from marseille or nice, not ajaccio. check that before you book anything
I was going to check that
I know. just saying it
Corsica on the 6th will be fine for climbing if the weather holds. Heavy rain there can last days. Maybe put a spare day on the end
good shout. spare day added
fine with the spare day as long as the spare day has cheese
Théo you don't get to decide the spare day
I can't sleep. Figue has decided that my keyboard is hers
Let her have it. Ours sleeps on the bed and it's worse
still awake. looked up the Corsica ferries at 4am which is a sign of something
Marseille to Ajaccio, how long is the night crossing? or is it Nice

Marseille to Ajaccio is around 8 to 9 hours overnight. Nice is longer and only runs in some seasons. Before anything else, check the van is allowed on the boat. Some operators charge a lot for vehicles over a certain height.
the van is 2.8m. I'm going to assume it fits
Assume less. Measure it.
i'll book the ferry once the sheet has the van height. dont book before we know the crossing times, i dont want to pay for a cabin we dont use
you're up?
sarah's alarm. she's on early. i'm up
I'm on the tram in 30 min, I'll put the height on the sheet
just got in. production office says we're fine for april 1st but the venue wants a tech day before that. so i'm there the 1st
i'm in the venue. don't tell me to check the sheet, i'm checking the sheet
Théo, you're not on the sheet yet. Camille, can you add who drives the van? Two drivers on the Marseille leg would help.
me and Inès. Inès you have a licence right
i have a licence. i'm not driving a camper for 9 hours on a motorway for free
I'll pay for the petrol Inès
you'll pay for the petrol and i'll sit in the passenger seat being right at you for 9 hours
Marking until nine. If anyone has the ferry timetable open, post it here and I'll look tomorrow morning.
booked nothing. crossing times are in a tab. marseille on the 5th and 6th, both leave late. the 6th arrives in ajaccio around 8am, which is a whole day lost if we want to climb that day
so we leave on the 5th and lose a night of verdon
or we skip the 5th night of verdon. same thing
ok I'm not angry about this I'm just annoyed
noted
ok reporting back from load out. the venue guy says he knows a climbing wall in ajaccio but it's "a bit scary." i asked if it's a bouldering gym and he said it's a rock. i think it's a cliff
THÉO it is a cliff
adding it to the sheet under "maybe, do not tell Inès"
i can read the sheet
Figue has gone to sleep on the sheet printout I left on the table. I'm going to let that stand
going to bed. Mathis, you were right about the van. I measured it. it's 2.9
2.9 is under the limit on the operator I checked. Check whether the roof rack counts before you book.
ferry site says height includes roof stuff. 2.9 with anything on the roof is tight
what's on the roof
nothing is on the roof. there's a bike rack I don't use
then 2.9 is fine. booking the 6th tonight, not before. do not message me at 2am
I'm on the tram. I'm not messaging anyone at 2am
tech day done. venue wants us back on the 1st at 8 for load in before the crowd. i can do a van leg but i need to be back in lyon by the 12th, there's a show
i'll drive if someone gives me a route with a cheese stop
the route has a cheese stop. it's called the Roquefort caves. you're welcome
😂 ok i'm sold
Camille, the Roquefort caves are not on the way from Marseille. Let's not pretend they are.
it's a 40 minute detour Mathis. the van can handle it
the van can handle it if the van is driven by someone who isn't me
booked the ferry. marseille to ajaccio, 6th, overnight, cabin shared. van 2.9 declared. confirmation is in the sheet tab "ferry (do not touch)"
you're a hero. I'm making you a tab
you already made a tab. i'm not a tab person
Marking done for the week. Sheet looks good. One question: do we keep a rest day in the Verdon before the crossing, or are we climbing up to the 5th?
home. read the sheet. rest day in bold so camille means it 😂
